summary.short: Shenzhen regulation on intelligent connected vehicles covering road testing and demonstration applications, product admission, registration, use management, infrastructure, network security, data protection and liability. Applies within the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone from 1 August 2022, as amended with effect from 1 July 2026.
summary.long: The regulation, adopted by the Shenzhen Municipal People's Congress Standing Committee on 23 June 2022 and effective 1 August 2022 (Art. 64), governs intelligent connected vehicles in the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone. A 2026 decision amended it with effect from 1 July 2026; this text is the consolidated version reprinted after that amendment. Vehicles are defined by three automation levels (conditional, high and full driving automation). Road testing and demonstration applications require filing, approval and temporary plates. Vehicles must be on the municipal product catalogue to be sold and on the registration system before road use, and must connect to a government supervisory platform and upload operating-safety data. Manufacturers must report safety defects and recall vehicles. Driver, owner and manager duties depend on automation level, and event data must be recorded for at least 90 seconds and stored for at least 30 days. Network security duties, a requirement to store data on servers within China with no outbound transfer without approval, and a ban on unlawful collection of user information apply. Accident liability is allocated by automation level. Penalties include seizure and fines of 100,000 to 500,000 yuan for unauthorised road testing.

notes: The document reproduces the 2026 amending Decision (adopted 2026-05-25, in force 2026-07-01), then the Regulation as amended. The Regulation was originally adopted 2022-06-23; Art. 64 gives its original commencement as 2022-08-01. Art. 1 refers generically to basic principles of laws and administrative regulations, and other references (国家有关标准, 国家有关主管部门) name no instrument, so no legal_basis or cross_references row is coded. The Decision ends with an unitemised note that individual wording was technically revised (此外，对个别文字表述作了技术修改), so the consolidated text cannot be fully checked against the Decision. Article renumbering follows the Decision's instructions.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment was found. Numbers in the text are penalty amounts and multipliers (Arts. 56, 57, 59, 60; enforcement), a one-year and three-year bar on re-application (Arts. 58, 59; enforcement), a ten-day notification period (Art. 29; deadline event), the 90-second recording and 30-day storage duties (Art. 37; content of an obligation), and the effective dates (Art. 64; events). The automation levels in Arts. 3 and 34 are classified by reference to national standards, not numeric cutoffs.
